question:
[MCQ] Based on the video clip, what is the operator trying to determine during the early targeted scan, and why?
A) Determine fetal presenting part to establish whether the fetus is head-down vs not
B) Identify placental location to assess for low-lying placenta or previa before proceeding with further obstetric imaging.
C) Confirm fetal cardiac activity and basic viability to ensure the fetus is alive during the initial targeted sweep.
D) Estimate amniotic fluid volume with a quick survey to screen for oligohydramnios or polyhydramnios early in the exam.
groundtruth: The operator immediately scans the lower uterine segment to identify the presenting part, confirming a cephalic (head-down) presentation by recognizing the fetal skull.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the video clip, which workflow step is being performed, and what is the next immediate objective?
A) Start with an overview plane, then sweep to map fetal lie/orientation along the maternal axis
B) Acquire a transverse fetal head plane to measure biparietal diameter, then confirm the cavum septi pellucidi and thalami are visible.
C) Identify placental location in a broad sweep, then assess for previa by evaluating the relationship to the internal cervical os.
D) Survey amniotic fluid qualitatively, then obtain a deepest vertical pocket measurement to screen for oligohydramnios/polyhydramnios.
groundtruth: After establishing an initial transverse view and checking the presenting part, the operator initiates a sweep to determine fetal lie and orientation relative to the maternal axis.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the video clip, what is the purpose of the broad sweep across the upper uterus with a curved follow-through motion?
A) Track the fetus to locate the end opposite the presenting part and confirm overall lie
B) Survey the fundal region to identify placental location and any retroplacental fluid collection
C) Perform a global sweep to estimate overall amniotic fluid volume and look for polyhydramnios/oligohydramnios
D) Reposition and align the fetus into a standard plane to obtain biometric measurements such as BPD or femur length
groundtruth: The operator sweeps across the fundus and curves around to follow fetal anatomy, locating the fetal buttocks at the uterine top and visualizing hips and legs to confirm the fetus is bum-up.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the video clip, what action is used to follow the target tissue boundary, and what is the main goal of this maneuver?
A) Slide the probe superiorly to trace the placental margin/body and confirm it is not low-lying
B) Fan/rock the probe in place to keep the placental edge centered, aiming to assess placental thickness and echotexture rather than its relationship to the internal os
C) Rotate to a transverse suprapubic view and sweep laterally to map the uterus, aiming to identify fetal presentation instead of confirming placental location
D) Apply color Doppler along the placental–myometrial interface to look for abnormal vascularity, aiming to evaluate accreta spectrum rather than low-lying placenta
groundtruth: The operator identifies the placental margin and then slides the probe superiorly to trace the placenta, confirming an anterior placenta and verifying it does not appear low-lying.
